newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei finishes at fresh high for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei finishes at fresh high for 1997.

text.p: The Tokyo Nikkei index finished at a high for 1997 for the second consecutive day, as buying of high-tech laggards, semiconducter-related shares and some issues driven by domestic demand provided support, brokers said.
The 225-share Nikkei average ended 48.40 points or 0.24 percent higher at 20,611.56. Its June futures shed 10 points to close at 20,550.
"Foreign investors absorbed the profit-taking moves by domestic institutional investors and propped up the indices," said Kenji Karikomi at Daiwa Securities.
Turnover at the end of the session was a modest 382 million shares, down from the 439 million traded the previous day.
Winners nudged ahead of losers 563 to 511, while 168 issues were unchanged.
Brokers said that major exporters such as Sony Corp were more or less in a consolidation phase and interest was shifting to issues which are second in line, such as Kyocera Corp.
The ceramic package maker's shares rose to a high for calendar 1997, adding 600 yen to 9,110.

"Passive component revenues should grow by 15 percent this year, and although near-term prospects for IC packaging are still mediocre it is clear that the business has bottomed out," said Joseph Osha, a Merrill Lynch Japan Inc vice president.
He added the Kyocera share price objective was 13,000 yen.
Shares in Advantest Corp, a semiconductor testing device manufacturer, also touched a high for the year before easing slightly to close 370 yen higher at 8,450.
Electronics trading firm Tokyo Electron Ltd rose 110 yen to 5,820. Brokers said semiconductor-related issues were gaining on a belief that the chip market has bottomed out.
Recent investor interest in real estate issues, stemming from hopes that land liquidity is on the road to recovery, spread to railway issues.
Keisei Electric Railway Co Ltd chugged 26 yen higher to 717 to become the most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse with trade totalling 5.59 million shares.
West Japan Railway Co also gained, added 4,000 yen to match its lifetime high of 439,000 yen.
Real estate issues were fairly firm with Mitsui Fudosan Co Ltd up 20 yen at 1,540.
Mitsubishi Estate Co Ltd rose 10 yen to finish at 1,680.

Services, retailers, electric equipment, credit/lease and communications topped the list of gaining sectors. Transport equipment, construction, mining, pharmaceuticals and miscellaneous manucfacturers headed the list of retreaters.
Banks also lost ground, helping to cap gains, brokers said.
"Dealers are active participants in the market and although the quest for individual issues is strong, trade direction is somewhat distorted," a trader at a second-tier brokerage said.
Market sources said they viewed the near-term target for the Nikkei average as being at the 21,000 level.

"The market is slowly approaching the point where it is starting to sound out the state of the economy in the latter half of the calendar year," said Masaaki Higashida, Nomura Securities strategist. "However, there are still too many uncertainties in the future to provide market participants with confidence."
In other indices, the TOPIX added 6.34 points or 0.42 percent to end at 1,518.27. The Nikkei 300 rose 1.38 points or 0.47 percent to 293.29.
The second-section index climbed 6.50 points or 0.36 percent higher to end at 1,795.13. Turnover was 12.12 million shares, compared to 10.35 million the precious day.

The over-the-counter index was up 1.42 points or 0.12 percent at 1,189.14 in late Tokyo. OTC debutant Megane Top Corp, which operates a chain of stores selling eyeglasses, rose to 3,060 yen from its 2,840 yen initial trade price.
Late in the afternoon Nissin Food Products Co Ltd said it would repurchase up to 13.3 million of its shares.
Nissin closed 90 yen higher at 2,910. --Masako Iijima, Tokyo Equities Desk (+81-3-3432-9052)
